findings_qualitative.value: Mdust/Mstar rises to z~2 then flattens; anti-correlated with Mstar up to z~5

evidence.quote: In both galaxy populations $M_{\rm dust}$/$M_{\rm \star}$ increases until $z\sim2$ followed by a roughly flat trend towards higher redshifts

claims.hypothesis: Mdust/Mstar differs between MS and SB DSFGs and evolves with z
claims.experiment: SED fitting of 300 ALMA-detected COSMOS DSFGs, binned by redshift
claims.result: SB have 3-4x higher Mdust/Mstar; both rise to z~2 then flatten
claims.finding: Mdust/Mstar separates MS and SB galaxies across redshift

evidence.quote: the SB DSFGs typically have $3-4$ times higher $M_{\rm dust}/M_{\star}$ as compared to MS DSFGs

claims.hypothesis: Cosmological simulation SIMBA reproduces observed Mdust/Mstar
claims.experiment: Compare SIMBA, P19 and B17 predictions with data
claims.result: SIMBA matches MS but underpredicts SB by factor 3-6; B17 and P19 agree
claims.finding: SIMBA needs faster dust growth/higher metallicity in starbursts

evidence.quote: SIMBA is less successful in reproducing the observed $M_{\rm dust}/M_{\star}$ in SB DSFGs and underpredicts this quantity by factor of 3-6

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Optically thick dust model gives 2-3x lower Mdust in highest-mass bin; DL14 optically thin masses kept for consistency

evidence.quote: For the sake of consistency, we thus keep our DL14-based $M_{\rm dust}$ for the rest of the paper.

limitations_admitted.value: Sample incomplete at fixed stellar mass because sources were preselected for ALMA follow-up

evidence.quote: We note that our sample is incomplete at fixed $M_{\star}$, since most of sources were preselected for the purpose of ALMA follow-ups.

referee_caveats_inferred: Mostly photometric redshifts; heterogeneous ALMA selection
